claims.head: Coyle’s line gets the soft minutes
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ L1 (Coyle, Olivier and Sillinger) spends at least 42% of its 5-on-5 time against the Panthers’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Coyle, Olivier and Sillinger) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would. That’s Rick Bowness chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Panthers’ second line is Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis.
claims.nums: At home: 42% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 24% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Panthers’ second line.

claims.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
claims.call: The Panthers’ power play creates at least their usual 7.9 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Blue Jackets’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Panthers’ power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Blue Jackets tonight.
claims.nums: Florida 8th for power play (7.9 expected goals per 60) · Columbus 29th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Panthers’ power play has a soft target in the Blue Jackets’ kill.

claims.head: The Blue Jackets’ defense joins the attack; the Panthers’ stays home
claims.body: On shots from defensemen, Columbus is one of the league’s best and Florida is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.gist: The Blue Jackets and the Panthers sit at opposite ends for shots from defensemen.
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Panthers’.

notes.text: Z. Werenski is out long term (shoulder injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
I. Provorov is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. C. Soucy has taken his spot beside D. Mateychuk.
D. Severson returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
D. Heinen has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
